title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

This page consolidates core company-handbook topics for Redwood Inference: an overview of what it's like to work here, roles and career ladders, benefits and perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and practical guides to the internal tools you will use in day-to-day work. This document is intended for new hires, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

1. Working at Redwood — principles and expectations

- Mission alignment: Our mission is to make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team. Employees are expected to prioritize customer-facing reliability and measurable performance improvements.
- Culture principles: shipping small, measuring impact, experimental rigor, psychological safety, and high-trust collaboration.
- Core working norms:
  - Asynchronous-first communication: prefer documented threads (Confluence, Slack with threads) for cross-team work.
  - Weekly demos: each team runs a 30-minute demo and prioritization sync.
  - Code review + automated tests required for all feature and infra changes.

2. Roles and career ladders

Short intro: Redwood maintains level definitions and career ladders for Engineering (IC and Manager tracks), Product, Design, SRE, and Customer Success. Each ladder defines expectations across four dimensions: impact, autonomy, craft, and leadership.

- Engineering IC levels (summary):
  - E1 (New grad / entry): contributes to well-scoped features, receives regular mentorship.
  - E2 (Engineer): owns components, independently delivers projects of medium complexity.
  - E3 (Senior Engineer): leads cross-component projects, mentors peers, influences architecture.
  - E4 (Staff Engineer): drives cross-team technical strategy, measurable platform improvements, and high-complexity design.
  - E5 (Principal): company-wide technical leader, represents Redwood externally for technical strategy.

- Manager track (summary):
  - M1 (Manager): owns a small team, people management, delivery and career growth of direct reports.
  - M2 (Senior Manager): multi-team coordination, program-level planning, and managers-of-managers readiness.

- Career growth process:
  1. Quarterly calibration: managers submit calibration packets with examples of impact and manager feedback.
  2. Career conversation: every employee has a 1:1 career conversation bi-annually with manager and a people-ops partner.
  3. Promotion packet: candidate prepares a narrative, 3-5 impact examples, and two peer/manager references.

3. Benefits and perks (summary table)

| Category | Redwood offering | Eligibility / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Health & wellness | Medical, dental, vision (US plans), global EAP, mental health stipend | All full-time employees; coverage begins on first day of employment for core medical plans where permitted |
| Time off | 25 PTO days (US baseline) + public holidays + 12 weeks parental leave | Flexible roll-over policy; capped at 40 days accrual |
| Financial | Competitive salary, annual bonus, equity grants, 401(k) with employer match (US) | Details in offer letter and People Ops portal |
| Learning & development | $2,000 annual L&D stipend, conference budget, internal mentorship programs | Requires manager approval for large external programs |
| Remote & hybrid | Stipend for home-office setup, co-working credits, periodic in-person offsites | Teams define recurring on-site cadence; people-ops coordinates company-wide events |
| Perks | Commuter benefits (where applicable), travel insurance for work trips, wellness stipends | See People Ops benefits portal for region-specific differences |

Benefits guidelines and processes:
- Enroll in benefits using the People Ops portal within 30 days of start date.
- Submit expense reimbursements for stipends via the expense system with receipts.

4. Hiring and onboarding overview

Intro: Hiring at Redwood is a collaborative process designed to evaluate role fit, technical skills, and cultural alignment while delivering a positive candidate experience. Onboarding is a 90-day program with clear checkpoints.

Hiring process (standardized steps):
1. Requisition & scorecard: hiring manager creates a role requisition with a public scorecard (must include core competencies and success criteria).
2. Sourcing & screen: TA screens candidates; phone screen (30 min) focused on fit and basics.
3. Technical assessment: role-appropriate exercise (take-home or live coding/architecture) administered by the interview loop owner.
4. Interview loop: 4-6 interviews including: hiring manager, peer engineer, manager, and cross-functional partner (product/design/security when relevant).
5. Debrief & calibration: interviewers complete written feedback; hiring manager runs a calibration meeting with TA and people-ops.
6. Offer & negotiation: TA extends offer; people-ops approves final compensation.

Onboarding program (90-day checkpoints):
- Day 0-7: pre-boarding checklist (IT account creation, laptop shipment, benefits enrollment instructions, Slack + Confluence access).
- Week 1: orientation week - company mission, product overview, security training, manager 1:1 schedule, buddy assigned.
- Week 2-4: role ramp - hands-on tasks, small deliverable, shadowing sessions with teammates.
- Month 1 check-in: manager and people-ops run a 30-minute checkpoint.
- Month 2: project ownership begins, career goals drafted.
- Month 3 review: 90-day review with manager, feedback from peers, and next-step plan.

Onboarding checklist (table):
| Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Laptop shipped & configured | IT | Before day 1 |
| Accounts provisioned (Slack, Google/GSuite, Confluence, Jira) | IT / People Ops | Day 0-1 |
| Security training completed | New hire | Day 7 |
| First small deliverable assigned | Manager | Week 2 |
| Buddy check-ins scheduled | Team | Week 1 |

5. Internal tools guide (quick reference)

This section lists the most common internal tools, owners, and brief usage notes. Detailed how-tos and troubleshooting pages are linked in the related pages section.

- Confluence (company documentation)
  - Purpose: canonical documentation repository for policies, runbooks, and design docs.
  - Owner: People Ops / Eng Docs
  - Best practices: create pages under the appropriate space, follow the Confluence template, include a short summary, owners, and related pages.

- Slack (team communication)
  - Purpose: real-time messaging and notifications.
  - Guidelines: use channels for topic-based discussion, threads for replies, avoid posting long-form decisions without Confluence link.
  - Policy: no sensitive customer data in public channels; use private channels or secure tickets for customer PII.

- Jira (ticketing & delivery)
  - Purpose: feature tracking, incident tracking (incidents use the incident template).
  - Practices: link PRs to Jira issues, write acceptance criteria, estimate in story points, and tag cross-team dependencies.

- GitHub (code & reviews)
  - Purpose: source control and CI.
  - Guidelines: required code review by at least one peer, passing CI, and release notes for major changes.

- People Ops portal (payroll, benefits, L&D)
  - Purpose: single place for benefits enrollment, payroll info, and learning budgets.
  - Contact: people-ops@redwood.example.com

- Internal playbooks & runbooks (SRE/ops)
  - Purpose: incident response, runbooks for common operational tasks.
  - Location: Confluence space "eng-sre" -> runbooks.

6. Manager responsibilities and handoffs

- Pre-hire: finalize scorecard, interview plan, and expected ramp timeline.
- Day 1-30: ensure onboarding checklist is complete, establish 1:1 cadence, set initial goals.
- Ongoing: quarterly performance conversations, promotion readiness reviews, and career development planning.

7. Useful templates and checklists (links & snippets)

- Offer checklist: role, compensation band, manager approval, equity grant, relocation stipend (if applicable).
- New-hire announcement template (Confluence + Slack snippet): includes role, manager, start date, buddy, and two-sentence summary of responsibilities.

8. Escalations and support

If a new hire is not ramping as expected, managers should: 
1. Schedule a 1:1 and document concerns.
2. Open a People Ops case and request support (mentorship, reduced scope, or performance plan).
3. Escalate to the hiring manager's manager and people-ops lead if progress is not observed within 30 days of plan initiation.

9. Ownership and contacts

- People Ops (onboarding, benefits, compensation): people-ops@redwood.example.com
- IT & workplace (equipment, accounts): it-support@redwood.example.com
- Recruiting / TA: recruiting@redwood.example.com
- Engineering Docs & Templates: eng-docs@redwood.example.com

10. Revision history and governance

- This document is maintained by People Ops and the Eng Docs working group.
- Review cadence: annual review or sooner for major policy changes.
- Change process: propose edits in a pull-request style Confluence draft, add reviewers, and move to published after approval.

Appendix: FAQs

Q: How do I request additional L&D budget?
A: Submit a ticket to People Ops with the program name, cost, learning objectives, and manager approval.

Q: Where are career ladder definitions stored?
A: See the linked pages under "related_pages" or navigate to /confluence/company-handbook/career-ladders.

Q: Who do I contact for urgent payroll issues?
A: Payroll team via people-ops@redwood.example.com with subject line "Payroll - Urgent".
